offers_products.reason: Manufactures pumps, valves, mechanical seals, actuators and controls as its core offerings.

offers_services.reason: Aftermarket services, repair, lifecycle services and monitoring are a major part, though smaller than new equipment.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Sells industrial flow control equipment to energy, chemical, power and water customers, not households.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Customers are oil and gas, chemical, nuclear power, mining, water utilities, contractors and engineers.

recurring_revenue.reason: Aftermarket parts, seals, repair and service are roughly half of sales and are repeat purchases; the rest is original equipment, so this is uncertain.

cyclical_demand.reason: Capital equipment for energy, chemical and industrial projects is often deferred in downturns, though aftermarket cushions.

big_ticket.reason: Many sales are seals, valves, parts and repairs bought frequently, though large engineered pumps are big projects.

people_delivered.reason: Revenue comes mainly from manufactured pumps, valves and seals rather than staff time.

large_customers.reason: Main customers are large oil and gas, chemical and power companies, nuclear operators and municipal water agencies.

asset_heavy.reason: Manufacturing and service centers are needed, but growth is not heavily capital intensive compared with utilities or fleets.

notes: Recurring share and asset intensity are borderline: the aftermarket is about half of sales, and manufacturing needs moderate capital.
